notes.title: Dev Blog #006
notes.notes: [p]Hey Supersonic Fighters![/p][p][/p][p]As my terrain rendering work has progressed, and since I now have full control over how the terrain is generated, I was able to add something I’ve been thinking about for a while. I could describe it...or I could just show you:[/p][p][/p][p]Before[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42909735/9a440f8fa66175ef6ec5cfcd6489b164f0aef91a.png"][/img][/p][p]After[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42909735/55bfa93728799849505a2a95eacc650f5a280cd2.png"][/img][/p][p]The F/A-18’s service ceiling is around 50,000 ft (15,000 m), and at that altitude, the Earth’s curvature is clearly visible. For reference, here’s a great YouTube video that lets you view Earth from different altitudes. Skip to 2m23s for what the horizon looks like at 10,000 m:[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="xpUcZXiKtfU;full"][/previewyoutube][p][/p][p]Curving my flat Earth was actually very easy BUT it did mean that the old Procedural Sky no longer worked because, of course, it has a flat horizon! So, and this will come as no surprise to you, I am currently creating my own sky shader.[/p][p][/p][p]If you'd like more updates, or you want to ask me any questions, be sure to join our Discord - and don't forget to wishlist Supersonic Fight![/p][p][/p][p]Rich[/p]

notes.title: Check Out the Brand-New Gameplay Trailer!
notes.notes:
Hey Supersonic Fighters!

I am very excited to share some new in-game footage with you! You can view it on the store page or directly here:

[previewyoutube=rOyXTT0cO_k;full][/previewyoutube]

Originally, I planned to have this trailer ready for Steam's "Planes, Trains, and Automobiles Fest" in September 2024. But, at the time, I wasn't happy with how the game looked - so I kept working on it until I was truly proud of the result.

The old video on the store page was the "Announcement Trailer", released way back in 2022. That video was more of a vision than actual game footage - fun fact: the carrier wasn't even moving, and the planes were hand-animated rather than flying!

For this new trailer, it was really important that everything you see is real - the flying, the physics of carrier landings, even the movement of the carrier itself. It's all happening in-game, in real-time.

If you would like to re-watch the original announcement trailer, here's a link:

[previewyoutube=_XL5ljcyXoU;full][/previewyoutube]

I'd love to hear what you think of the new footage! If you'd like more updates, be sure to join our Discord - and don't forget to wishlist Supersonic Fight!

Rich

notes.title: Dev Blog #005
notes.notes:
Hey Supersonic Fighters!

A few weeks ago, I shared an image of the “low-res terrain,” showing what the distant scenery will look like—here it is again:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42909735/896d452c9793121a49de3238a865ec590fdf2f6d.jpg[/img]

Since then, I’ve been working on the “high res terrain” — the ground you’ll actually be flying over and seeing up-close. The game will include very large areas (San Francisco being the obvious one), so I needed to automate the process as much as possible.

I had done a lot of work on this some time ago, creating procedural tools to adjust terrain height and paint textures. I even made a video about it back in Dec 2022:

[previewyoutube=cDxPgcaBIIo;full][/previewyoutube]

However, those tools were very slow, which made it hard to tweak things and immediately see the results. To fix that, I switched to Compute Shaders—super-fast tools that let me see terrain changes instantly. It has completely transformed the workflow.

Anyway, enough talk. Here’s an image that gives you an idea of what the terrain will look like up-close:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42909735/d5872b6cc02103bb41749afdd34fab3a38939c4f.png[/img]

Let me know what you think! If you’d like more updates, hop into our Discord—and don’t forget to wishlist Supersonic Fight!

– Rich

notes.title: DEV BLOG #002: SUPERSONIC FIGHT - BACK TO BASICS
notes.notes:
Hey Supersonic Squadron, 

I’ve been working on some exciting new features: from recording replays for PVP to fighting the uncanny valley on behalf of Supersonic Fight’s NPCs (have you ever noticed how little attention is paid to NPCs in sim games?!).

For a change of pace, and to rigorously test these new developments, I swapped the beloved F/A-18 Hornet jets of our actual game for the classic charm of Sopwith Camel biplanes - a nostalgic nod to aviation history. This choice isn't just a whimsical deviation; it's a testament to the freedom and creativity that being a solo developer affords me - the power to blend history with modern gaming tech. Dive into the video below to witness this fusion of past and present. I would love to hear what you think of this!

[previewyoutube=0MeglDFanBQ;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1][b]SUPERSONIC (DOG)FIGHT[/b][/h1]

Not only will the final version of the game feature these magnificent men in their flying machines as a playable option, but it will also include a PVP or team dogfight experience. The video above showcases an intriguing glimpse into this aspect – watch as the planes engage in an intricate aerial ballet, demonstrating the sophisticated flight modeling I've been fine-tuning. What makes this even more special is knowing that every maneuver and aerial dance you see was captured directly from a game-testing session.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42909735/32485e81912ee82b9727ffda1bce7bd096ac9caa.gif[/img]

notes.title: Dev Blog #001
notes.notes:
(This is the first Dev Blog entry that was posted on our Discord server. Come and join!)

I was working on another project in January 2022 (that project was "secret_vr_project"). I had already created a helicopter flight model which was relatively easy and I wanted to add a fixed wing flight model. "How hard could that be?" - I wondered. As it turns out: really, really, REALLY hard!

I was using an F18 as my placeholder jet and, as I was setting it up, I was reminded of the reason I first wanted an Amiga. Picture the scene - it's 1987 or 1988, I am in the back of my parents car, driving home from Wales. I am flicking through a computer magazine when I stumble upon screenshots for an upcoming game "F/A-18 Interceptor" by Bob Dinnerman: 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42909735/a23245d199e3100e6fd387a599f1dccfcafde6cd.png[/img]

As someone who had played Commodore 64 games for 4 years (Microprose's F19 Stealth Fighter and Gunship for example), these images were mind-blowing. I had to have this game. So began a relentless plan to convince my parents that I must have a Commodore Amiga 500. By Christmas 1989, my strategy of annoying my parents paid off and, like many others, I received the Commodore Amiga 500 Batman pack. Guess what game happens to be included in that pack?

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42909735/0033d56f5ff7c27e18c27999a27a85217c484721.jpg[/img]

What can I say? Christmas '89 was the best Christmas ever! (Seriously - it has never been topped.) Like so many others, I flew an F18 around the San Francisco Bay Area, under the Golden Gate Bridge, around the weird shaped thing (which I now know was Sutro Tower - a radio tower) and completed a set of missions, fighting back an unknown enemy. ( I say "unknown"...but this was during the Cold War so we all knew who the enemy was meant to be).

Back to January 2022, I thought to myself: "I wonder if I could re-create the feeling of F/A-18 Interceptor"? ...and here we are!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42909735/1404ba5f0f58f0a1bb239b515522482377b79f27.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42909735/a170dfc74c2a9cb64f2304d1f224f7b4e30afa27.png[/img]

Join me! it's gonna be a lot of fun!
